Undated candidate topics for the blog queue. Nothing here is scheduled. The queue scheduler locks a candidate into a Wed/Sat slot ~14 days before publish, filtered by eligibility window and cannibalization distance, and only if approved. Replaces the practice of dating a year of content up front — see plans/ blog content queue redesign (2026-08-04).

CANDIDATE SHAPE. Required: slug, title, primary_keyword, status, source. The scheduler's candidateToPost() also reads description, topic_type, search_intent, funnel_stage, conversion_goal, related_cluster, page_role and refresh_cycle - it defaults each one, so a candidate missing them still schedules but publishes with generic metadata. check-data-integrity.js warns on those so a hollow entry is visible before it occupies a slot. seasonality_window must be a name from content-taxonomy.json (lifecycle.seasonal.seasonality_windows) or null; anything else is INELIGIBLE ON EVERY DATE since the filter started failing closed, so the build errors on an unknown value rather than letting it sit unschedulable. research_brief carries the researcher's SERP evidence, differentiation angle, direct-answer target, questions, entities and sources; candidateToPost passes it to the dated post, blog-planner injects it into the blog-write task, and seo-auditor's draft gate verifies the draft against it.

candidates.title: Why Kentucky Home Insurance Rates Are Rising and What to Do Now
candidates.description: A plain-language breakdown of why Kentucky homeowners are paying more in 2026 and the concrete steps an independent agent can take to reduce your premium without cutting coverage.
secondary_keywords: why is my home insurance going up kentucky
how to lower home insurance kentucky

research_brief.demand_evidence: Live search confirms intense media coverage: Insurance.com data shows Kentucky had a 10.6% single-year increase and an average premium of $4,471, placing it eighth-highest in the nation. Newsbreak (Sep 17, 2026) reports Kentucky saw a 33% year-over-year jump, ranking it among the steepest increases nationally. Ramsey Solutions puts the 2026 Kentucky average at $3,795. Spectrum News 1 (May 14, 2026) ran a dedicated story on rising premiums hitting Kentucky families. This is live news driving active searches.
research_brief.serp_landscape: Page 1 is dominated by LendingTree, ValuePenguin, Bankrate, NerdWallet, MoneyGeek, and Insurify. Every result is a national aggregator presenting statewide averages with no Bullitt County or Daviess County detail, no independent agent voice, and no actionable local guidance. One competitor post from Boswell Insurance Agency (Murray, KY) ranks with a detailed 2026 cost report but covers western Kentucky. No post addresses Bullitt County or the Louisville-suburb market specifically.
research_brief.differentiation_angle: A post anchored in the I-65 corridor and Bullitt County growth story, citing local factors (new construction in Shepherdsville and Mt. Washington, wind and hail deductible shifts specific to the region, the KFB-vs-independent comparison context) beats aggregators on local relevance. The agency can cite real renewal patterns it sees from clients, which no aggregator or out-of-market agency can replicate.
research_brief.direct_answer_target: Kentucky home insurance premiums rose 10.6% in 2026, pushing the state average to roughly $4,471 per year, one of the highest in the nation. The main drivers are severe weather losses, rising rebuild costs, and roof-age surcharges. An independent agent who shops multiple carriers can often reduce that increase by 10 to 25 percent at renewal.

research_brief.local_angle: Bullitt County is experiencing active new construction (Mallard Lake, Wildwoods, Wray Estates subdivisions in Shepherdsville and Mt. Washington), meaning many homeowners are insuring brand-new homes and may not realize their policy limit needs to reflect current rebuild costs, not purchase price. The I-65 corridor also sees higher commuter traffic and weather exposure than rural Kentucky, which affects underwriting. The Way Agency can speak to what carriers are actually writing in the Shepherdsville ZIP code right now.

candidates.title: Insurance for Plumbing Contractors in Kentucky: A Complete 2026 Guide
candidates.description: A Kentucky-specific guide covering every coverage type plumbing contractors need to license, bid jobs, and protect against water damage claims, with the actual state minimums from DHBC regulations.

research_brief.demand_evidence: The agency already has a plumbing contractors industry page (/industries/plumbing-contractors.html) and the published HVAC and roofing contractor insurance guides have performed well as a cluster. The plumbing guide is the missing sibling. Live SERP shows ContractorNerd, MoneyGeek, and allenthomasgroup.com rank for 'plumbing contractor insurance Kentucky', while rbisomerset.com (a Kentucky independent agency in Somerset) has a targeted post. The agency's existing product page and industry page give it entity authority to rank for a dedicated blog post targeting this query family.
research_brief.serp_landscape: Page 1 is mixed: ContractorNerd (national, data-heavy, cost-focused), MoneyGeek (aggregator), allenthomasgroup.com (out-of-state independent agency with a Kentucky-specific page), rbisomerset.com (Kentucky independent agency, thin post), and ServiceTitan (trade software). No post combines the Kentucky DHBC licensing insurance minimums (the $250,000 GL minimum from 815 KAR 20:080 for master plumbers), completed operations coverage detail, water damage liability, and a working Kentucky agent's perspective. The allenthomasgroup page is the strongest competitor but is a generic agency not located in Bullitt or Daviess County.
research_brief.differentiation_angle: A post grounded in Kentucky Revised Statute KRS Chapter 318 and 815 KAR 20:080, explaining the $250,000 GL minimum for master plumber licensing, the surety bond considerations for plumbing contractors, the specific water damage and completed operations exposure Kentucky plumbers face in the cold-weather months (freeze-thaw burst pipes along the Ohio River valley), and The Way Agency's real access to specialty carriers that restrict plumbing work will beat every generic national guide.
research_brief.direct_answer_target: Kentucky plumbing contractors must carry at least $250,000 in general liability insurance to hold a master plumber or plumbing contractor license under 815 KAR 20:080. Most working contractors carry $1 million per occurrence to meet GC contract requirements. Workers compensation is also required for any employee under KRS 342.630. Completed operations and water damage liability are the two coverage gaps that cause the most denied claims.

research_brief.local_angle: Kentucky plumbers face a freeze-thaw exposure unique to the Ohio River valley and Bullitt County climate, where burst pipe emergencies spike from November through February. New construction in Shepherdsville and Mt. Washington means more residential plumbing jobs on freshly built subdivisions, where a botched connection caught months later triggers a completed operations claim. The Way Agency knows which carriers will write plumbing in Kentucky without a plumbing exclusion, which is the most common coverage gap this agency sees in contractor policies written elsewhere.

candidates.title: Small Business Health Insurance in Kentucky: Options for Fewer Than 10 Employees
candidates.description: A practical breakdown of every health coverage option available to Kentucky businesses with fewer than 10 employees, including SHOP marketplace access, QSEHRA, ICHRA, and the Small Business Health Care Tax Credit.
candidates.primary_keyword: health insurance small business less than 10 employees kentucky
secondary_keywords: small business health care tax credit kentucky

research_brief.demand_evidence: The query 'health insurance for small business with less than 10 employees' appears in the dossier's top performers section at position 1.0 with a 100% CTR, indicating the site has already served this intent. This is a strong signal to expand the cluster with a dedicated, long-form guide. The planned 'group-health-insurance-small-business-kentucky' post targets the general 'group health insurance small business kentucky' keyword but does not specifically address the sub-10-employee context, which has distinct product eligibility rules (QSEHRA maximum benefit caps, SHOP tax credit threshold at fewer than 25 FTE, and the full-credit threshold at fewer than 10 FTE). These are different enough to justify a separate post.
research_brief.serp_landscape: Page 1 is owned by PeopleKeep, forhealthinsurance.com, eHealthInsurance, Anthem, and Kentuckiana Insurance Group. National platforms dominate. The kynect SHOP marketplace angle and Kentucky-specific carrier availability (Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield as the primary 2026 SHOP carrier per forhealthinsurance.com) are present in national guides but the nuanced under-10-employee tax credit rules (full credit at fewer than 10 FTE averaging under $27,000 per year) are either missing or buried. No local Kentucky agent page ranks on page 1 for this query family.
research_brief.differentiation_angle: A post that leads with the SPECIFIC answer that businesses with fewer than 10 employees and average wages under $27,000 per year may qualify for the FULL Small Business Health Care Tax Credit (worth up to 50% of premiums paid through kynect SHOP), then walks through the QSEHRA and ICHRA alternatives for businesses that do not meet SHOP minimums, with Kentucky carrier details (Anthem, WellCare), will be the only result that directly answers the sub-10-employee question with Kentucky-specific program names, thresholds, and local agent guidance.
research_brief.direct_answer_target: Kentucky businesses with fewer than 10 employees are not required to offer health insurance, but several affordable options exist. The kynect SHOP marketplace lets businesses with 1 to 50 employees access Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield group plans, and businesses with fewer than 25 employees averaging under roughly $65,000 in wages may qualify for a federal tax credit worth up to 50 percent of premiums paid. Businesses too small for group coverage can use a QSEHRA or ICHRA to reimburse employees for individual plans tax-free.

entities_to_cover: Small Business Health Care Tax Credit (ACA)
QSEHRA (Qualified Small Employer Health Reimbursement Arrangement)

research_brief.local_angle: Small businesses along the I-65 corridor in Bullitt County and in Owensboro compete with Louisville and Evansville employers for workers. Offering even a modest health benefit through a QSEHRA or SHOP plan is a competitive advantage in the Shepherdsville and Mt. Washington labor market, where new businesses are forming alongside the residential construction boom. The Way Agency can act as a licensed navigator for kynect SHOP and help owners compare group and HRA options without steering them to a single carrier.

candidates.title: Home Insurance for Shepherdsville Homeowners: A Bullitt County Rate Guide
candidates.description: A Shepherdsville-specific home insurance guide covering what homeowners in Bullitt County pay in 2026, what new construction neighborhoods need to know, and how an independent agent shops more carriers than Farm Bureau or State Farm alone.

research_brief.demand_evidence: The dossier shows the zipcode '40165' (Shepherdsville's primary ZIP) at position 8.0 with 100% CTR, signaling the site already gets found for this geographic intent. Live SERP for Shepherdsville home insurance is dominated by lead-generation tools (vhomeinsurance.com, gethomeinsurancequotes.com with outdated rate data), Kentucky Farm Bureau agent pages (Cheryl Day, North Agency), and a State Farm agent page. One local independent agency, Kentucky Bred Insurance, has a Shepherdsville home insurance post but is not in Bullitt County and presents thin content. The site's existing Shepherdsville location page gives domain authority for a supporting blog post.
research_brief.serp_landscape: Page 1 features: vhomeinsurance.com (stale rate data, no agent voice), gethomeinsurancequotes.com (quote aggregator, outdated $998 average), Kentucky Farm Bureau's Cheryl Day agent page (captive, biased toward one carrier), a State Farm agent page, kybredinsurance.com (thin, out-of-area agency), and Yellow Pages. No comprehensive, updated, independent-agent-authored Shepherdsville home insurance guide exists on page 1. This is an open door for a local agency with the existing Shepherdsville location page to anchor a blog post.
research_brief.differentiation_angle: A post that cites current 2026 rate benchmarks (the statewide average is $4,471 per year per Insurance.com, compared to what an independent agent can often find for Shepherdsville's ZIP code), addresses the specific new construction considerations in Mallard Lake, Wray Estates, and Wildwoods subdivisions (replacement cost accuracy on new builds), explains wind and hail percentage deductibles that have replaced the traditional flat $1,000 deductible across most Kentucky carriers, and positions The Way Agency's multi-carrier access against the captive KFB and State Farm agents on page 1 will win on both relevance and local trust.
research_brief.direct_answer_target: Home insurance in Shepherdsville, KY costs roughly $800 to $1,300 per year for an average home, though 2026 statewide rate increases mean older homes and those with aging roofs may pay significantly more. Bullitt County homeowners can often lower their premium by shopping across multiple carriers, a task independent agents handle without charging extra. New construction in Shepherdsville requires special attention to replacement cost accuracy and percentage wind and hail deductibles.
